question_text:
**Comprehension (Q. 96 - 100):** Hughie Erskine was charming and generous, but had little money and no successful profession. He wished to marry Laura, yet her father insisted that Hughie must first obtain a respectable income. One day, Hughie visited his friend Alan Trevor, a painter who was completing a portrait of an elderly beggar dressed in torn clothes. The model appeared so weak and miserable that Hughie felt immediate sympathy for him. While Alan briefly left the room, Hughie searched his pockets and found a single gold coin. Although he could scarcely afford to lose it, he placed the coin in the beggar's hand. The old man thanked him with unusual courtesy. Later, Alan informed Hughie that the supposed beggar was Baron Hausberg, one of the wealthiest men in Europe. The baron had deliberately posed as a poor man for the painting. Hughie was deeply embarrassed. He imagined that the millionaire would laugh at his foolish attempt to offer charity. The following morning, however, a representative of the baron arrived with an envelope. It contained a substantial sum of money described as a wedding gift from "an old beggar." The incident reveals the difference between wealth and generosity. Hughie possessed very little, yet he was prepared to share it without expecting recognition or reward. The baron, though rich, valued the sincerity of the act because it had been performed under the belief that he was helpless. Charity offered for public approval may flatter the giver, but compassion shown in private reveals character.

---

Why did Laura's father hesitate to approve her marriage to Hughie?
option_a: He doubted Hughie's ability to remain generous after marriage.
option_b: He disliked Hughie's friendship with the painter Alan Trevor.
option_c: He expected Hughie to establish a respectable source of income.
option_d: He believed Hughie lacked sufficient affection and concern for Laura.
